data.title: TDS Cloaking Behavior Detection
data.description: Detects domains serving divergent content based on visitor attributes such as geolocation, device fingerprint, or user agent, a technique known as cloaking. TDS operators serve benign or empty content to security scanner user agents (e.g., Googlebot, bingbot, crawlers), datacenter IP ranges, and known security vendor IP addresses, while delivering redirects or malicious content to residential IP addresses and consumer device fingerprints. This rule identifies cloaking by correlating response divergence across multiple request profiles to the same URL: when a domain returns substantially different HTTP response codes, content lengths, or redirect targets for scanner versus residential visitor profiles within a detection window, it indicates intentional cloaking. Supports TP-0042 Phase 3 detection of TDS cloaking used to evade automated threat scanning and URL reputation systems.

detection.condition: selection and scanner_response and residential_response and content_divergence

enrichment_required.source: WHOIS enrichment (target domain registration date lookup)

falsepositives: Geo-restricted content delivery serving different pages by region legitimately
A/B testing platforms serving variant content to different visitor segments
Bot management solutions intentionally serving CAPTCHAs to automated traffic
